title: Do we need to attend lectures
titleChinese: 大学生是否需要听讲座式课程？
paragraphs: At some point in our lives, most of us have attended a school or university lecture. These learning sessions give us some insightful nugget of knowledge or can be something we yawn through, trying to keep awake. Whatever our experience, lectures have been and still are the most common teaching method in education. But will they exist in the future?

With the growth of the internet and so much information at our fingertips, you may think there is no need to gather together at a fixed location clutching a handful of textbooks. BBC journalist Matt Pickles, says "research has shown that students remember as little as 10 per cent of their lectures just days afterwards."

Professor Carl Wieman, who campaigns against the traditional lecture, felt talking at students and expecting them to absorb knowledge was not that effective so he introduced 'active learning' that encourages problem solving in small groups. He listens to them and guides their discussions. The result has been improved exam results. Other new alternatives to the lecture have included peer-to-peer learning and project-based learning that enable students to link up and work collaboratively on projects such as building a computer game.

Sometimes the lecture room is not conducive to learning; a boring, colourless room is not necessarily an inspiring place for stretching the mind. At the Massachusetts Institute of Technology two lecture rooms have been refitted to allow students to sit around small tables with screens showing animated simulations to help them visualise concepts.

But new learning methods can come at a high financial cost compared to the relatively cheap way of being taught face-to-face by an academic. The real issue according to Professor Dan Butin, founding dean of the school of education and social policy at Merrimack College in Massachusetts, is that "Academics put thousands of hours of work into their books and much less time into thinking about the effectiveness of their teaching style." But he says "the lecture has survived because research, not teaching, determines the success of a university and its academics."
So if research quality is a measure of a university's success and money is tight, then the lecture could be here for a little longer. How does that make you feel? How would you improve your lectures?

vocabulary.entry: insightful [adj.] /ˈɪnsaɪtfəl/ 有深刻见解的；富有洞察力的
vocabulary.example: She gave an insightful analysis of the situation.
vocabulary.translation: 她对形势做了有深刻见解的分析。

vocabulary.entry: nugget [n.] /ˈnʌɡɪt/ 有价值的信息；珍品 (比喻)
vocabulary.example: The book contains many nuggets of wisdom.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书包含许多智慧的点滴。

vocabulary.entry: link up [phr.] /lɪŋk ʌp/ 连接；联系；联合 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The two companies linked up to share resources.
vocabulary.translation: 这两家公司联合起来共享资源。

vocabulary.entry: collaboratively [adv.] /kəˈlæbərətɪvli/ 合作地；协作地
vocabulary.example: They worked collaboratively on the project.
vocabulary.translation: 他们在这个项目上合作。

vocabulary.entry: conducive to [phr.] /kənˈdjuːsɪv tuː/ 有利于；有助于 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: A quiet environment is conducive to study.
vocabulary.translation: 安静的环境有利于学习。

vocabulary.entry: visualise [v.] /ˈvɪʒuəlaɪz/ 形象化；想象 (英式拼写，美式: visualize)
vocabulary.example: Try to visualise your goals as already achieved.
vocabulary.translation: 试着把你的目标想象成已经实现的样子。

vocabulary.entry: at one's fingertips [phr.] /ət wʌnz ˈfɪŋɡətɪps/ 触手可及；随时可用 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: With a smartphone, information is at your fingertips.
vocabulary.translation: 有了智能手机，信息触手可及。

vocabulary.entry: absorb knowledge [phr.] /əbˈzɔːb ˈnɒlɪdʒ/ 吸收知识 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Children absorb knowledge like sponges.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子像海绵一样吸收知识。

vocabulary.entry: peer-to-peer learning [n.] /ˌpɪə tə ˈpɪə ˈlɜːnɪŋ/ 同伴学习 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Peer-to-peer learning encourages collaboration.
vocabulary.translation: 同伴学习鼓励合作。

vocabulary.entry: project-based learning [n.] /ˈprɒdʒekt beɪst ˈlɜːnɪŋ/ 基于项目的学习 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Project-based learning develops practical skills.
vocabulary.translation: 基于项目的学习培养实践技能。

vocabulary.entry: stretch the mind [phr.] /stretʃ ðə maɪnd/ 拓展思维；开阔思路 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Reading philosophy stretches the mind.
vocabulary.translation: 阅读哲学能拓展思维。

vocabulary.term: come at a high financial cost [phr.]
vocabulary.entry: come at a high financial cost [phr.] /kʌm æt ə haɪ faɪˈnænʃəl kɒst/ 带来高昂的经济成本 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The new equipment came at a high financial cost.
vocabulary.translation: 新设备带来了高昂的经济成本。

vocabulary.entry: be tight [phr.] /biː taɪt/ 紧张的；拮据的 (指资金)
vocabulary.example: The budget is very tight this month.
vocabulary.translation: 这个月的预算很紧张。

vocabulary.entry: determine the success of [phr.] /dɪˈtɜːmɪn ðə səkˈses əv/ 决定……的成功 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Hard work often determines the success of a project.
vocabulary.translation: 努力工作往往决定项目的成功。

vocabulary.entry: a measure of [phr.] /ə ˈmeʒər əv/ 衡量……的尺度；一定程度的
vocabulary.example: Test scores are a measure of student progress.
vocabulary.translation: 考试成绩是衡量学生进步的尺度。

vocabulary.entry: campaign against [phr.] /kæmˈpeɪn əˈɡenst/ 反对；开展反对……的运动 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: They campaigned against the new law.
vocabulary.translation: 他们开展运动反对新法律。

vocabulary.entry: expect sb to do sth [phr.] /ɪkˈspekt ˈsʌmbədi tuː duː ˈsʌmθɪŋ/ 期望某人做某事 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The teacher expects students to complete their homework.
vocabulary.translation: 老师期望学生完成作业。

vocabulary.entry: refit [v.] /ˌriːˈfɪt/ 改装；重新装备
vocabulary.example: The room was refitted with new furniture.
vocabulary.translation: 房间重新配备了新家具。

vocabulary.entry: animated simulation [n.] /ˈænɪmeɪtɪd ˌsɪmjʊˈleɪʃən/ 动画模拟 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Animated simulations help explain complex processes.
vocabulary.translation: 动画模拟有助于解释复杂的过程。

vocabulary.entry: effectiveness [n.] /ɪˈfektɪvnəs/ 有效性；效果
vocabulary.example: The effectiveness of the treatment is well known.
vocabulary.translation: 这种治疗的有效性是众所周知的。

sentences.english: At some point in our lives, most of us have attended a school or university lecture.
sentences.chinese: 在我们生命中的某个时刻，我们大多数人都参加过学校或大学的讲座。

sentences.english: These learning sessions give us some insightful nugget of knowledge or can be something we yawn through, trying to keep awake.
sentences.chinese: 这些学习课程教授我们一些有深刻见解的宝贵知识，或者也可能是我们打着哈欠、努力保持清醒熬过的东西。

sentences.english: Whatever our experience, lectures have been and still are the most common teaching method in education.
sentences.chinese: 无论我们的经历如何，讲座一直以来都是，并且仍然是教育中最常见的教学方法。

sentences.english: But will they exist in the future?
sentences.chinese: 但它们在未来还会存在吗？

sentences.english: With the growth of the internet and so much information at our fingertips, you may think there is no need to gather together at a fixed location clutching a handful of textbooks.
sentences.chinese: 随着互联网的发展，大量信息触手可及，你可能会认为没有必要在一个固定的地点聚在一起，手里还抓着几本教科书。

sentences.english: BBC journalist Matt Pickles, says "research has shown that students remember as little as 10 per cent of their lectures just days afterwards."
sentences.chinese: BBC记者马特·皮克尔斯说：“研究表明，学生们在听完讲座几天后，仅仅只能记住其中的10%。”

sentences.english: Professor Carl Wieman, who campaigns against the traditional lecture, felt talking at students and expecting them to absorb knowledge was not that effective so he introduced 'active learning' that encourages problem solving in small groups.
sentences.chinese: 卡尔·维曼教授反对传统的授课方式，他认为对着学生讲话并期望他们吸收知识并不是那么有效，所以他引入了“主动学习”方法，鼓励学生以小组形式解决问题。

sentences.english: He listens to them and guides their discussions.
sentences.chinese: 他倾听并指导他们的讨论。

sentences.english: The result has been improved exam results.
sentences.chinese: 结果是学生的考试成绩提高了。

sentences.english: Other new alternatives to the lecture have included peer-to-peer learning and project-based learning that enable students to link up and work collaboratively on projects such as building a computer game.
sentences.chinese: 其他替代传统讲座的新方法包括同伴学习和基于项目的学习，这些方法使学生能够沟通联系，在诸如制作电脑游戏等项目上合作开展工作。

sentences.english: Sometimes the lecture room is not conducive to learning; a boring, colourless room is not necessarily an inspiring place for stretching the mind.
sentences.chinese: 有时，教室并不有利于学习；一个枯燥、毫无色彩的房间不一定是扩展思维的好地方。

sentences.english: At the Massachusetts Institute of Technology two lecture rooms have been refitted to allow students to sit around small tables with screens showing animated simulations to help them visualise concepts.
sentences.chinese: 在麻省理工学院，有两个教室经过了改装，让学生们可以围坐在小桌子旁，屏幕上展示着动画模拟，以帮助他们形象化理解概念。

sentences.english: But new learning methods can come at a high financial cost compared to the relatively cheap way of being taught face-to-face by an academic.
sentences.chinese: 但是，与教师面对面教学这种相对便宜的方式相比，新的学习方法可能会带来高昂的经济成本。

sentences.english: The real issue according to Professor Dan Butin, founding dean of the school of education and social policy at Merrimack College in Massachusetts, is that "Academics put thousands of hours of work into their books and much less time into thinking about the effectiveness of their teaching style."
sentences.chinese: 马萨诸塞州梅里马克学院教育与社会政策学院的创始院长丹·布廷教授认为，真正的问题是“学者们投入数千个小时在他们的著作上，而花在思考自己教学方式有效性上的时间却少得多。”

sentences.english: But he says "the lecture has survived because research, not teaching, determines the success of a university and its academics."
sentences.chinese: 但他也说：“课程之所以能延续下来，是因为决定一所大学及其学者成功的是研究，而不是教学。”

sentences.english: So if research quality is a measure of a university's success and money is tight, then the lecture could be here for a little longer.
sentences.chinese: 所以，如果学术研究质量是衡量一所大学成功的标准，而且资金紧张，那么课程可能还会存在一段时间。

sentences.english: How does that make you feel?
How would you improve your lectures?
